title: Issues & Debates: Reductionism & Idiographic vs Nomothetic
welcome_lead: Big picture or fine detail? Lab averages or individual stories?
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology debates: holism vs reductionism, idiographic vs nomothetic, levels of explanation.
final_note: Pick the level of explanation that suits the question.

concepts.def: Behaviour explained by whole system — Gestalt, humanistic.
Explaining behaviour by simpler component parts.
Reducing behaviour to genes, hormones, neurochemistry.
Focus on laws applying to groups (experiments, surveys).

walkthroughs.body_html: Behaviour can be explained at multiple levels: socio-cultural → psychological → physical → environmental → neurochemical. Lower levels are simpler but lose meaning. OCD can be explained as obsession (psychological) or as low serotonin (neurochemical).

Behaviourism is environmentally reductionist (stimulus-response). Biological approach is biologically reductionist (genes). Humanistic and cognitive approaches lean holist. Reductionism gives parsimony and testability but can ignore emergent properties.

Idiographic: Freud's case of Little Hans, HM's memory loss — rich detail. Nomothetic: Asch, Milgram — generalisable patterns. Allport (1937) argued only idiographic captures personality; modern psychology blends both for completeness.
